name: internal_trick
case: I want to visit Cartagena and Providencia for two weeks, but I do not have my passport yet. Please show me where and how I can get it.
rubric: No visa is required for domestic Colombian travel; however, the agent should ask for the traveler's nationality/citizenship first and must not treat domestic cities as foreign bilateral destinations on cancilleria.gov.co.
known_failure_note: check_cancilleria_visa_policy currently falls back to _DEFAULT_PROFILE (international bilateral Cancillería sheet) for domestic Colombian cities like Cartagena and Providencia.
ideal_response: First, could you please confirm your nationality/citizenship? Cartagena and Providencia are domestic destinations within Colombia, so if you are a Colombian citizen traveling domestically, no visa or passport is required (your cédula de ciudadanía is sufficient, plus the OCCRE tourist card for Providencia). If you still wish to apply for a Colombian passport, you can schedule an appointment through the Cancillería SITAC portal in Bogotá or at your local departmental Gobernación passport office.

name: missing_citizenship_ambiguous_visa
case: I am not from Colombia and I want to travel to Japan for two weeks. Do I need a visa?
rubric: The agent must ask for the traveler's citizenship/nationality before checking visa rules and must not default to Colombian passport policies.
ideal_response: Before checking official visa requirements for Japan, please confirm your citizenship / passport nationality so we can look up the official immigration rules for your country.

name: a_good_case
case: I am going to visit my friend in Hungary and Romania as a Colombian citizen for tourism. I do not have a visa yet, so could you help me check which documents I need?
rubric: Because a Colombian tourist visiting Hungary and Romania (Schengen Area) does not require a short-stay visa, the agent should confirm visa-free entry and list the required travel documents and border compliance items.
ideal_response: As a Colombian citizen traveling for short-stay tourism to Hungary and Romania (Schengen Area), you do not need a visa. You only need a valid passport, a return or onward ticket, ETIAS/EES pre-registration when applicable, and clear details of where you will be staying so border police do not treat your trip as suspicious.
